title: Coping with Stress-Affected Personnel, and Implementing It for Better Teamwork
canonical_question: Stress is one of the factors affecting the performance of an individual. What are the primary strategies that may be employed for coping with stress-affected personnel? How can these strategies best be implemented among a ship's personnel so as to motivate them for better teamwork?
present_day_examinable_core: A two-part human-element question whose second part depends on the first, so it is one answer and not two. Part one asks for STRATEGIES for coping with stress-affected personnel - which must be organised as a hierarchy, strongest control first, not offered as a list of kindnesses. Part two asks how the same measures are IMPLEMENTED on a ship and how doing so builds a motivated team. The present-day framework has moved materially in the candidate's favour since this wording was last set: the 2022 amendments to MLC 2006 entered into force on 23 December 2024 and gave the answer hard legal anchors it did not previously have - social connectivity, prompt medical disembarkation, and an express prohibition on shipboard violence, harassment, sexual harassment, bullying and assault.

recommended_exam_depth.note: MIW's recommendation for a whole-question answer in two dependent parts. The sittings that evidence this family print a paper total only, with no per-question split, so no mark here is inherited from any examiner's paper.

understand_first: This question looks soft and is marked hard. The trap is that it invites sympathy - 'talk to the man, be understanding, encourage teamwork' - and sympathy is not a strategy. What turns it into a management answer is a HIERARCHY OF CONTROL, exactly as for any other hazard: remove the stressor if you can, control it by organisation if you cannot, support the individual only after those two, and treat the medical case as a medical case. A Chief Engineer who reorganises the work so that a man is not doing forty hours of unplanned maintenance on top of a watch has done more about stress than any amount of counselling. The second thing to hold onto is that the second half of the question is not a separate topic. It asks how 'these elements' - the coping strategies - are implemented so as to motivate for teamwork; the answer is that the measures that reduce stress are the same measures that build a team, because both come down to fair workload, clear authority, competence, being listened to, and being able to speak up without cost. Say that connection out loud. It is the sentence the question is fishing for.

blocks.h: Four sections, and put the hierarchy in writing

blocks.p: Head the answer What stress does to performance, The stressors on a ship, The strategies, in order of strength, and Implementation, and why it motivates a team. Naming the hierarchy explicitly - eliminate, control, support, treat - is what lifts this from a welfare essay to a management answer.

ul: Open with the mechanism. One short paragraph on how stress degrades attention, judgement and risk perception, and therefore safety. That earns the right to everything after it.

Anchor it in instruments. ISM for the management duty, MLC 2006 as amended for the entitlements - including the 2022 amendments in force since 23 December 2024 - STCW for rest hours and for leadership competence, and the IMO fatigue guidelines. Candidates who write this question with no instrument in it lose the professional marks.
Separate fatigue from stress but link them. They are different mechanisms with a common cause in workload, and the examiner rewards the distinction.
Be concrete about implementation. Named actions a Chief Engineer takes - the work plan, the handover, the toolbox talk, the appraisal, the reporting culture - not aspirations.
Close on measurement. How you would know it had worked. Very few candidates do this and it is a strong finish.

blocks.h: 1. Why stress is a safety question, not a welfare question

blocks.p: Stress is the response to a demand that exceeds, or is felt to exceed, a person's capacity to meet it. A little arousal improves performance; beyond an optimum it degrades it, and the degradation is selective in the worst possible way. Attention narrows, so the scan of the plant becomes a stare at one gauge. Working memory shortens, so steps in a procedure are dropped. Judgement becomes short-term, so the quick fix beats the correct repair. Risk perception blunts, so a permit is skipped. Communication contracts, so the man who has spotted something says nothing.

Chronic stress adds physical and behavioural effects - disturbed sleep, illness, irritability, withdrawal, and increased use of alcohol or tobacco - and eventually anxiety and depression. The result is a person who is present but unreliable, which is more dangerous than an absent one, because the watch system assumes they are functioning. That is why casualty investigation so consistently finds the human element behind the technical cause, and it is why this is a Chief Engineer's problem and not the Company doctor's.

Distinguish stress from fatigue. Fatigue is the deficit left by insufficient rest or excessive duty; stress is the strain of demand exceeding capacity. They are separate mechanisms and they feed each other - stress spoils sleep, and lost sleep lowers the threshold at which demand becomes stress - so they usually have to be attacked together, and the same measures often serve both.

blocks.h: 2. The stressors that are specific to a ship

ul: Workload and manning - a reduced crew against a rising burden of planned maintenance, inspections, audits, vetting, port State control and reporting.
Watchkeeping and disturbed sleep - split rest, night calls, unmanned machinery space alarms, port work on top of a sea watch.
Confinement and isolation - long contracts, no shore leave, the same forty faces, and separation from family at exactly the moments that matter.
Poor connectivity - being unable to reach home, or reaching home and being unable to do anything about what you hear.
Multicultural and multilingual crews - miscommunication, differing norms of deference and of raising a concern, and hierarchy that discourages speaking up.
Inspection and blame pressure - the fear that a finding becomes a personal fault, and the fear of criminal exposure after a casualty or a pollution incident.
Job insecurity and money - contract renewal, promotion, wage delay, family debt.
Bullying, harassment and discrimination, including sexual harassment - now expressly prohibited under MLC 2006 as amended.
Exposure to danger - transit of a high-risk or conflict area, piracy, heavy weather, or the aftermath of a serious accident or a death on board.
Environmental load - noise, vibration, heat and motion, which raise the physiological cost of every task and are themselves regulated for exactly that reason.

blocks.p: This is the core of the answer. The order is the point: a strategy lower on the list is a mitigation of a stressor that a strategy higher up should have removed.

headers: What it looks like on the ship
rows: 1. Eliminate or reduce the demand
Attack the stressor itself. The only complete answer

Realistic planned maintenance loading; deferring non-critical work with the Company's agreement rather than in silence; riding squads and shore assistance for heavy jobs; enough hands for the job actually being done; automation and condition monitoring to remove routine burden; cutting duplicated reporting
2. Control by organisation
Change how the work is arranged so the demand lands survivably

Watch and rest patterns that comply with STCW Code A-VIII/1 and MLC and are audited against what was actually worked; rest protected before critical operations; sequencing port work so that the same men are not on both ends of it; job planning with toolbox talks and proper handover; clear authority and lines of communication as the ISM Code requires, so nobody carries a decision that is not theirs
3. Build capacity
Raise the capacity side of the equation instead of only lowering demand

Familiarisation on joining; competence-based training and drills so that the unusual event is rehearsed rather than improvised; mentoring and cross-training so one person is not the single point of failure; the leadership, teamworking and managerial competences STCW requires at management level - taught and used, not merely certificated
4. Detect early
Stress is visible if anyone is looking

Know your people well enough to notice the change - withdrawal, irritability, uncharacteristic error, absence, deteriorating appearance, loss of humour, alcohol. Use the routine one-to-one, the appraisal and the informal conversation deliberately. Encourage peers to report a concern about a shipmate as a safety observation, not as telling tales
5. Support the individual
Once identified, act - and act proportionately

A private, unhurried conversation that establishes the cause rather than delivering a lecture; temporary reallocation of duty away from safety-critical tasks; protected rest; help with the actual problem, which is often a phone call home or a shore-side administrative fix; the Company's welfare or employee assistance provision and the 24-hour seafarer helplines; welfare, chaplaincy and seafarers' centre contact in port; and shore leave, which is the oldest and most effective single measure
6. Treat the medical case as medical
Judgement about competence is management; diagnosis is not

Telemedical advice; the ship's medical guide; and where immediate care is needed, prompt disembarkation and access to medical facilities ashore - which the 2022 amendments to MLC 2006 made an express obligation. Repatriation on medical grounds where the case requires it, and a fitness-for-duty decision recorded rather than assumed
7. Review
Close the loop, or the same stressor returns next voyage

Include workload, hours of rest and near-miss data in the SMS review; raise a non-conformity where manning or planning is the root cause, so that it reaches the Company as a system finding and not as one man's difficulty

blocks.p: The two things not to do. Do not manage a stressed man by giving him less responsibility permanently and never discussing it - that reads as demotion and adds a stressor. And do not treat it as a discipline matter until you have established that it is not a capacity matter; disciplining a man for errors caused by a workload you set is both unjust and useless.

blocks.h: 4. The framework this sits inside - and what it now requires

ul: ISM Code. The safety management system must be resourced and manned, personnel must be familiarised and trained, and the Company must establish defined levels of authority and lines of communication and ensure personnel can communicate effectively in their duties. Reporting of non-conformities, accidents and hazardous occurrences, and the Company's own review and evaluation, are the machinery through which a workload problem becomes a corrected problem.

MLC 2006, as amended. Hours of work and rest, minimum manning, accommodation, food and catering, medical care, shore leave, repatriation and access to welfare facilities. The 2022 amendments entered into force on 23 December 2024 and matter directly here: recreational facilities and amenities must include social connectivity, with reasonable access to ship-to-shore telephone and internet where available; there is a new obligation to ensure prompt disembarkation of seafarers needing immediate medical care and access to treatment ashore; the health and safety provisions now expressly prohibit shipboard violence, harassment, sexual harassment, bullying and assault, with preventive policies and safe reporting mechanisms required; and personal protective equipment must be of an appropriate size for the wearer.

STCW as amended. The minimum hours of rest and their exceptions; fitness for duty, including the alcohol limit; and, at management level, the competences in leadership and managerial skill and in engine-room resource management - which is the formal name for most of what this question is asking about.

IMO Guidelines on fatigue, MSC.1/Circ.1598 (24 January 2019). The current IMO guidance, addressed in separate modules to the seafarer, the master, the Company and the Administration, and expressly intended to be taken into account in developing and maintaining the safety management system, in training, and in casualty investigation. It is guidance, not a mandatory instrument, and should be named as such.

blocks.h: 5. Implementing it - and why the same measures motivate a team

blocks.p: The second half of the question. The honest answer is that stress reduction and team motivation are not two programmes; they are the same actions seen from two sides. Every measure below does both jobs.

rows: Publish a realistic weekly work plan and defend it with the Company
Removes uncertainty and the sense of an infinite list
Everyone can see the job is shared out fairly, which is the single largest driver of engine-room resentment
Brief every significant job - toolbox talk, risk assessment, permit, who does what and who stops the job
Removes ambiguity, which is a stressor in itself
Gives each hand a defined and visible contribution instead of a pair of hands
Delegate real responsibility with real authority, to the level of competence
Reduces the CE's own overload, which is a stressor the department feels
Recognition and growth are the strongest motivators available at sea, and they cost nothing
Protect rest and record hours honestly
Directly attacks fatigue and the guilt of falsified records
Signals that the rules apply to management too. Nothing corrodes a team faster than a rest-hour record everybody knows is fiction
Run a genuine no-blame reporting culture - thank the reporter, act visibly, feed the outcome back
Removes fear of consequence, the most under-recognised stressor on a ship
Turns the crew into the safety system rather than its subject
Train and drill deliberately, including the emergencies the department owns - blackout, engine-room fire, flooding, steering failure
Competence is the cheapest anxiety reducer there is
Shared rehearsal is what makes a group act as a crew under load
Insist on a working language and use plain, checked communication, standard phrases where a common language cannot be assumed, and closed-loop confirmation of orders
Prevents the misunderstanding that becomes an incident and then a blame
Includes everybody, and removes the quiet exclusion that multilingual crews suffer
Take an interest in connectivity, food, accommodation and shore leave, and press them as management issues
These are the actual entitlements MLC protects, and the actual causes of most misery
Demonstrates that the department's welfare is defended upward, which is what earns discretionary effort
Appraise fairly, mentor cadets and juniors, and mark completed work as completed
Replaces open-ended pressure with achievement
Progression and belonging - and the reason people stay with a fleet
Set the example on hours, temper, drink and standards
A stressed and short-tempered Chief Engineer is a stressor for the whole department
Leadership on a ship is imitated, not announced

blocks.h: 6. How you would know it worked

blocks.p: Finish with evidence, because a management answer that cannot be measured is an intention. Watch the near-miss and hazard-report rate (it should rise before anything else improves, because people have started speaking), rest-hour exceptions, overtime and deferred planned-maintenance backlog, the repeat-defect rate and unplanned work, sickness and medical repatriations, retention and re-joining rate, drill performance, and the pattern of findings at internal audit, port State control and vetting. Report the trend to the Company through the SMS review, so that the fix survives your relief.

Almost every candidate can list ways of being nice to a stressed shipmate. Very few produce a hierarchy of control, name the instruments, distinguish stress from fatigue, or answer the second half of the question as an implementation problem rather than a repeat of the first half. Those four things are where the marks are, and the last of them is where most answers simply stop.

ul: Answering with a motivation theory. The question is about coping with stress-affected personnel and then implementing those measures. Maslow and Herzberg are relevant background, but a question about stress answered as a lecture on the hierarchy of needs has changed the subject - and MIW's solved QP2512 Q4 already answers the Maslow question properly, so a candidate who wants that material should read it there.

Writing it with no regulation in it. This is a management-level examination. ISM, MLC as amended, STCW and the IMO fatigue guidelines all bear on it, and the 2022 MLC amendments in force since 23 December 2024 are the newest and most citable material available.
Treating discipline as a stress strategy. Until you have established that the errors are not caused by the workload you set, discipline is both unjust and ineffective. Say so - examiners notice it.

blocks.h: What this answer deliberately does not claim

ul: It quotes no rest-hour figures in the body. They are in the critical-numbers card, sourced to a competent-authority restatement rather than to a text MIW holds under licence, so a candidate can see exactly how strong that claim is.

It gives no MLC Standard or Guideline numbers for the 2022 amendments beyond naming the subject matter of each. The substance - social connectivity, prompt medical disembarkation, the express prohibition of violence and harassment, appropriately sized PPE - is established and dated. MIW has not read the amendment instrument at source, and a mis-numbered Standard in an answer script is worse than a correctly described one with no number.
It does not claim MSC.1/Circ.1598 is mandatory. It is guidance, and it says so.

blocks.p: MIW's solved corpus answers several neighbouring human-element tasks and they are worth reading beside this entry rather than instead of it: the human element in the STCW Code with the IMO fatigue guidance; the broad IMO and ILO regimes on maritime labour and welfare; Maslow's theory applied on board; fitness for duty for watchkeeping personnel; and multinational communication with crew management after repeated PSC failure. None of them answers the printed task here - primary strategies for coping with stress-affected personnel, and their implementation for teamwork - which is why this entry was authored.

quick_revision.recall_15s: Stress narrows attention, shortens memory, shortens judgement and blunts risk perception - so it is a safety problem. Answer as a hierarchy: eliminate the demand (realistic PMS, manning, riding squads); control by organisation (rest patterns, planning, clear authority per ISM); build capacity (training, mentoring, ERM and leadership competence); detect early (know your people); support the individual (private conversation, reallocation, welfare and helplines, shore leave); treat the medical case medically (telemedical advice, prompt disembarkation under the 2022 MLC amendments); then review through the SMS. Implementation and motivation are the same actions: fair workload, briefed jobs, real delegation, protected and honest rest hours, no-blame reporting, drills, a working language, and defending welfare upward. Measure it by near-miss rate, rest-hour exceptions, backlog, sickness and retention.
critical_numbers: 23 December 2024 - entry into force of the 2022 amendments to MLC 2006, which added social connectivity, prompt disembarkation for immediate medical care, the express prohibition of shipboard violence, harassment, sexual harassment, bullying and assault, and appropriately sized PPE
24 January 2019 - MSC.1/Circ.1598, the current IMO Guidelines on fatigue, which superseded the 2001 guidance

Minimum hours of rest under STCW Code A-VIII/1 - not less than 10 hours in any 24-hour period and 77 hours in any 7-day period, the 10 hours divisible into no more than two periods of which one is at least 6 hours, and intervals between rest periods not exceeding 14 hours. These figures are carried in MIW as a competent-authority restatement, not from a text MIW holds
quick_revision.critical_regulation: ISM Code - resources and personnel, familiarisation and training, defined levels of authority and lines of communication, effective communication, reporting of non-conformities and hazardous occurrences, and Company review. MLC 2006 as amended - hours of work and rest, manning, accommodation, food, medical care, shore leave, repatriation and welfare, with the 2022 amendments in force from 23 December 2024. STCW as amended - minimum hours of rest, fitness for duty, and the management-level competences in leadership and managerial skill and in engine-room resource management. MSC.1/Circ.1598 - IMO Guidelines on fatigue, GUIDANCE and not mandatory.
quick_revision.major_trap: Answering the second half of the question by repeating the first, or answering the whole question as a motivation theory. The second half asks how the coping strategies are implemented among the ship's personnel so as to motivate for teamwork - so it must name actions and show that the same action does both jobs.

authority_sources.source: MLC 2006 as amended, including the 2022 amendments to the Code adopted by the Special Tripartite Committee in May 2022, approved by the 110th session of the International Labour Conference and in force from 23 December 2024 - social connectivity within recreational facilities and amenities; prompt disembarkation of seafarers requiring immediate medical care and access to medical facilities ashore; express prohibition of shipboard violence, harassment, sexual harassment, bullying and assault with preventive policies and safe reporting; appropriately sized personal protective equipment
authority_sources.checked: Established as at 24 August 2026 and dated: the amendments were approved at the 110th session of the International Labour Conference in June 2022 and entered into force on 23 December 2024, so they are OPERATIVE law and not a future item. The SUBJECT MATTER of each amendment relied on here was verified; MIW has NOT read the amendment instrument at source and therefore cites no Standard or Guideline number for them, which is declared in the study guide. The underlying entitlements relied on elsewhere in the answer - hours of work and rest, manning, accommodation, food and catering, medical care, shore leave, repatriation, access to welfare facilities - are the unamended substance of the Convention.

authority_sources.source: ISM Code - safety and environmental protection policy, resources and personnel including familiarisation and training, defined levels of authority and lines of communication, ability to communicate effectively, reporting and analysis of non-conformities, accidents and hazardous occurrences, and Company verification, review and evaluation
authority_sources.checked: Read at source and confirmed in force and unamended in substance as at 24 August 2026. Cited for the management duties it actually creates. The Code says nothing about stress by name, and this answer does not pretend that it does: what it supplies is the resourcing, authority, communication, reporting and review machinery through which a workload problem becomes a corrected one.

authority_sources.source: STCW 1978 as amended - Code section A-VIII/1 minimum hours of rest and their exceptions, regulation VIII/1 fitness for duty including the alcohol limit, and the management-level competences in leadership and managerial skill and in engine-room resource management
authority_sources.checked: Confirmed in force as at 24 August 2026. Cited for the rest-hour obligation and for the fact that leadership, teamworking and resource management are CERTIFICATED COMPETENCES at management level rather than optional soft skills - which is the point that makes this a management-level answer. The comprehensive review of the Convention and Code is in progress and is recorded under not_yet_in_force, because nothing from it is adopted.

authority_sources.source: Minimum hours of rest figures under STCW Code A-VIII/1 - not less than 10 hours in any 24-hour period and 77 hours in any 7-day period; the 10 hours divisible into no more than two periods of which one is at least 6 hours; intervals between consecutive rest periods not exceeding 14 hours
authority_sources.checked: Carried at the class MIW already uses for the Manila rest-hour figures elsewhere in the corpus, and consistent with those existing records. MIW does not hold the STCW Code text under licence, so the figures rest on national maritime administration guidance restating the Convention rather than on the Convention text read at source, and they are labelled accordingly. They are kept out of the answer body and confined to the critical-numbers card so that the strength of the claim travels with the figure.

authority_sources.source: MSC.1/Circ.1598, 24 January 2019 - IMO Guidelines on fatigue, approved by MSC 100 and superseding the guidance approved in 2001
authority_sources.checked: Confirmed as at 24 August 2026 to be the current IMO fatigue guidance, with its date and its supersession of the 2001 guidance established. Cited as GUIDANCE and expressly not as a mandatory instrument, including its own statement that it should be taken into account in developing and maintaining safety management systems, in training, and in casualty investigation.

authority_sources.source: Occupational stress management practice applied to a ship - the stressor/strain model, the degradation of attention, working memory, judgement and risk perception under excessive arousal, the distinction between stress and fatigue, and the hierarchy of control (eliminate, control by organisation, build capacity, detect, support, treat, review)
authority_sources.checked: Settled human-factors practice with no governing instrument, declared as such. It is framework-independent and unchanged, and it is the organising structure of the answer rather than a citation: no instrument prescribes a hierarchy of control for stress, and this entry does not attribute one to any.

not_yet_in_force: The comprehensive review of the STCW Convention and Code is in progress at IMO and NOTHING from it is adopted or in force. It is expected to reach an adoption meeting - an extended Maritime Safety Committee session or a diplomatic conference - around 2027, and among the workstreams carried forward is one on fatigue and hours of work and rest. A candidate may say that the review is under way and may not say that anything it produces is a requirement.
superseded_framework: The IMO guidance on fatigue mitigation and management approved in 2001 was superseded by MSC.1/Circ.1598 of 24 January 2019. Older notes on this subject still cite the 2001 guidance and it should not be presented as current.

review_record.reviewer: Laptop Claude Code (independent clean-context review pass)
review_record.notes: Reviewed against the question and the cited authority. FIVE checks. SCOPE: the printed task has two limbs and the second depends on the first - 'how these elements can be best implemented ... motivating them for better team work' - so the correct treatment is ONE answer, not two independent limb answers, and the entry is scoped whole for that reason rather than for convenience. That decision was tested the other way and it fails the other way: a standalone limb on implementation would have no referent for 'these elements'. Section 5 does the joining work explicitly, in a table that gives each action both a stress reason and a team reason, which is the exact thing the printed wording asks for and the thing most answers omit. CURRENTNESS is the real value added here, and it is dated: the 2022 amendments to MLC 2006 entered into force on 23 December 2024, which is AFTER every sitting that evidences this family, so the family's answer today is materially better resourced than it was when the wording was last set. Social connectivity, prompt medical disembarkation and the express prohibition of violence and harassment are all in force and all directly on point. Correctly presented as operative law rather than as a future item. NUMBERS: three, all dated and all sourced, and the rest-hour figures are deliberately confined to the revision card under a COMPETENT_AUTHORITY_RESTATEMENT label consistent with how the rest of the MIW corpus carries them. No MLC Standard or Guideline number is quoted for the 2022 amendments, and the entry says why - MIW did not read the amendment instrument. That is the honest treatment and it was checked specifically, because inventing 'Standard A3.1 paragraph 2' would have been the easy way to look authoritative. AUTHORITY HONESTY: MSC.1/Circ.1598 is labelled guidance, not a requirement; the ISM Code is expressly stated NOT to mention stress by name; the hierarchy of control is attributed to human-factors practice and to no instrument. Each of those three is a place where an answer could have over-claimed and does not. FAILURE MODE CHECKED DELIBERATELY: that this had not quietly become the Maslow answer. It has not - motivation theory appears only in the study guide, and only to point the candidate at MIW's existing solved QP2512 Q4 rather than to duplicate it. PASS.

version_history.reason: First publication under QI Phase-2 tranche 003. QIF-EM-0043 is a NEW_MODERN_ANSWER_REQUIRED family with nine sittings across six years and no MIW answer. The reuse order was applied and the nearest solved candidate, QP2512 Q4 on Maslow's theory of motivation, was read in full and REJECTED as owner: it answers motivation theory and the Chief Engineer's response to lack of motivation, and it does not address strategies for coping with stress-affected personnel, which is the first and governing limb of this question.
version_history.authority: MLC 2006 as amended including the 2022 amendments in force 23 December 2024; ISM Code read at source; STCW as amended for rest hours, fitness for duty and the management-level leadership and resource-management competences; MSC.1/Circ.1598 of 24 January 2019 as current IMO fatigue guidance; human-factors practice for the hierarchy of control.

next_review_trigger: Re-review when the comprehensive review of the STCW Convention and Code reaches adoption, since its fatigue and hours-of-work workstream bears directly on this answer; or if the ILO adopts further amendments to the MLC Code affecting health protection, medical care, accommodation or connectivity; or if IMO supersedes MSC.1/Circ.1598. Also re-review if MIW solves a past paper that sets coping with stress-affected personnel directly, in which case the relationship between that sitting-anchored answer and this one must be adjudicated rather than assumed. Routine re-review at twelve months, because two of the three instruments behind it are actively moving.
